messages:
sre_bot: INCIDENT 🚨 severity=high auth.login.errors > 25% in us-west, eu-west (1915001234) — possible external IdP failures. Paging oncall.
alex.chen: I'm seeing spikes in 502/504 on token verification paths. Console login flows failing. quick checks: auth-proxy logs show upstream okta introspect 502s.
maya.patel: Support reporting multiple customers can't sign into the console since ~08:12 UTC. CS thread showing SLO breaches. Can anyone confirm whether this is Okta or our side?
jordan.kim: digging now. curl to introspect endpoint from prod edge:
```
$ curl -i -X POST https://okta.company.introspect/token -d 'token=***'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:14:10 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"upstream_unavailable","details":"timeout contacting jwks service"}
```
alex.chen: logs show repeated JWKS fetch failures: `jwks_client: fetch failed 503` then `jwt: verification failed: no matching kid`. So either Okta's JWKS endpoint flapping or our caching is broken.
priya.singh: We have a local JWKS cache fallback built into auth-proxy (last refreshed ~07:00 UTC). Can we toggle policy to prefer cache when upstream returns 5xx? I can prepare the rollout. Risk: slightly stale keys for rotated certs, but safer than 100% login failures.
maya.patel: Agree. Escalating to product and CS for an incident banner. Prepare status message recommending console login workaround (SSO via company VPN) if possible.
alex.chen: Proposed mitigation steps:
1) set AUTHZ_JWKS_FALLBACK=prefer-local on auth-proxy config
2) increase local cache TTL to 10m
3) enable throttled retries to Okta with backoff
I can apply the config change and do a canary to us-west-prod first.
sre_bot: deploy_bot triggered: creating canary job for deployment/auth-proxy
deploy_bot: canary started on node pool: auth-canary-1 (1915001700)
jordan.kim: running the env update:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/auth-proxy AUTHZ_JWKS_FALLBACK=prefer-local AUTHZ_JWKS_TTL=600 --record
```
priya.singh: Watch logs for any auth failures that mention `stale-key` — if we see that, roll back fallback immediately.
alex.chen: Canary looks good for 4 minutes — user logins processed, token verifications passing via cached keys. No immediate `stale-key` errors.
maya.patel: Oncall handoff: I'm taking over monitoring and comms. Jordan, please keep the rollout progressing to eu-west and ap-southeast as long as canary holds.
jordan.kim: rolling to eu-west and ap-southeast now (1915001890 -> 1915002000). Progressing.
support_jenn: CS update drafted: "We're investigating intermittent login failures affecting console access. We're deploying a mitigation to prefer cached authentication keys to restore access while we work with Okta. We'll update in 30 minutes." Want me to post?
product_tom: yes please post to status.redwood.ai and notify top 10 paying customers via the incident channel.
alex.chen: Metrics: login success rate recovered from 72% -> 98% within 7 minutes of canary -> global rollout. Token introspect 5xx rate dropped to baseline.
maya.patel: Good. Next steps: 1) keep fallback for 30m while Okta stabilizes, 2) engage Okta support with request id and logs, 3) prepare post-incident notes and timeline.
priya.singh: Opening a support ticket with Okta (case #REQ-5621) and attaching jwks fetch logs and timestamps. Also asking for root cause ETA.
jordan.kim: Noted one customer showed `jwt: kid not found` even after fallback — reached out directly to CS to gather user details for possible rotated key scenario.
sre_bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied globally at 08:21 UTC. Monitoring continues. Next status in 30m (1915002134).
alex.chen: Handing off to maya for the next hour. I'll stay available if we see regression. Postmortem required, likely third-party root cause + gap in JWKS error handling.
maya.patel: Acknowledged handoff. I'll keep monitoring and will coordinate the post-incident writeup with Priya and Alex. Posting initial banner now. :white_check_mark:
support_jenn: Status page updated and top customers notified. CS queue watching.
product_tom: Thanks all — good mitigation. We'll need a follow-up to add better telemetry around JWKS fetch latencies and an automated fallback test in our chaos-suite.
alex.chen: adding to infra board: `AUTH-47` (improve jwks cache and fallback testing). Closing thread when Okta confirms stability and we revert fallback.
